card.name: Hasapiko
card.era: Medieval (Byzantine-era origin as a butchers' battle mime)
card.tagline: The 'butcher's dance' of Constantinople; basis of sirtaki.
card.profile: A Greek folk dance from Constantinople, originating in the Middle Ages as a sword/battle mime by the Greek butchers' guild, adopted from the Byzantine military; historically called makellarikos horos. The slow version (hasapikos varys, 'heavy') is in 4/4; the fast version (grigoro hasapiko or hasaposerviko) in 2/4. Danced in a short line/open circle, hands on neighbours' shoulders, with synchronized steps; accompanied by bouzouki and rebetiko-era ensembles. Sirtaki is a modern choreographed version of it (English Wikipedia; Dance Museum).
card.insight: The hasapiko is the structural basis of the 1964 sirtaki; its fast, Balkan-influenced form is the hasaposerviko (English Wikipedia, citing Leontis, 'Culture and Customs of Greece').
